What can you say honestly makes you, you?
Nobody else thinks exactly like I do.
The individual experiences I've gone through in life and how I've handled them, in situation to situation basis.
Haha alright, well if you were to classify certain experiences that had the most meaning to you, which would rank among the most significant?

hmmm I'd say the 6 years of highschool/middleschool dealing with losing my grandmother whom I'd always lived with to Cancer slowly. Taught me a lot and propelled me into making something of my life or at least trying to.
How does one lead to the other? If I'd lost my grandmother like that at that age, it'd probably cause me to be more cynical/reclusive. Thanks for sharing this btw.

my grandmother was never bitter about her condition. She prayed everyday and loved everyone she met she would've given you the shirt off her back if it meant it would make you more comfortable, the summer she went into recommission was my Sophomore year and we spent the summer constantly going places, to the river, or to the movies or even to another town just to go to yard sales and garage sales, and she was so happy, she was later diagnosed with a more aggressive cancer that she still stayed positive about. The last thing she said to me was "Have fun, don't be too sad and I love you" and I live by that. She lived beautifully and I aim to spend my life doing or at least trying to do the same.

I've had a lot of time throughout all of it to cope with it, sharing helps others I think.

I think I agree that you're helping others this way. You don't have to share if it's not something you want to talk about, but what were/are the more difficult aspects of coping? That doesn't sound like something that ever just "goes away"

Honestly It's been two years and I still wake up and expect to be in the house I grew up in and seeing her there. I still expect to get up on sunday mornings to go to church with her and I still have yet to delete her phone number out of my contacts and I replay her old voicemails I have. I watched the strongest bravest most amazing woman I have ever known and ever will slowly wither away to nothing. Watching the sickness weaken her and taking away her ability to be her we couldn't go into the backyard and pick blackberries because with chemo and radiation she wasn't allowed to be in direct sunlight for prolonged periods of time which was also difficult in it's own because we spent most of the time outside, it was difficult but I was there and I tried so hard to help her because that's what love is. She loved her life and I would go out of my way to make sure it was easier for her to love her life. And on occasion I find cancer jokes distasteful although I know they're in no way directed towards my situation and it's not that I find them offensive, just distasteful.

Again, thank you for sharing this. You've been one of the more genuine people I've met here. I admire your thick skin. However, I hope you don't forget that there are other people around who's ear you can bend if you need it. I've seen too many instances where people try to put on a happy face and keep that face on for too long. It's hard to watch how it chews at their insides.

Yes I find more often than not people are openly willing to listen to your sad story and to try and help you. I never fake a smile because happiness is a genuine thing and I appreciate that. And thank you, I don't mind sharing at all. In my church I went through emotional therapy training to be there for the kids in the class I teach, so I share this story a lot. Admittedly the first few times are hard to share something like that but I can smile now because at least she didn't live the last 6 years of her life sad and depressed like most people would.
